title: The Kindness Meter
rule: A number above everyone's head counts how many times they've helped someone.
logline: In a city where a glowing number over every head counts your good deeds, the only person stuck at a red zero is the one who never helps for an audience — and when meteors fall, he's the only one who stays.
hook_card: In this world, a number floats above everyone's head showing how many times they've helped someone, and mine was stuck at zero.
title_options: Everyone Had Thousands. He Had Zero.
His Kindness Meter Was Stuck at Zero… Until the Meteors Hit
hook_caption: Everyone had thousands. He had a red zero. Then the meteors came. ☄️
description: In a city where a glowing number above your head counts every time you've helped someone, everyone has thousands — except one kid with a red 0. Shops slam doors on him. VIPs mock him. Then a server-wide meteor storm hits, the top helpers run for their rare pets, and the zero is the only one who stays. Watch it twice: the clue is two frames long.
pinned_comment: Be honest: if this number floated over YOUR head right now, would it be high… and would it be real? 👇

hero.name: Me (the Zero)
hero.bio: Narrator. Mid-teens, hoodie, quiet. Helps people only when nobody's around — so his meter has never moved off a red 0. Want: one point, one person who doesn't flinch. Flaw: has stopped expecting anyone to.

vo.name: Narration (his voice)
vo.bio: First-person voice-over: calm, close, a little tired.

guest.name: Guest
guest.bio: A brand-new default character: blank grey, dot eyes, meter at 2. The only person who doesn't read the number before the face.

luxe.name: Luxe
luxe.bio: #1 on the leaderboard (9,882). Helps beautifully — the moment a phone comes up.

vance.name: Vance
vance.bio: #2 (8,410). Shades at night. Believes the number is the person.

bram.name: Mr. Bram
bram.bio: Owner of TOYS. Reads numbers, not faces. Holds the door at the end — and says nothing.

mom.name: Shopper
mom.bio: Won't take help from a zero. Will take it from a camera.

oldman.name: Old Man Pell
oldman.bio: Gets 'helped' a lot. Mostly on camera.

setting_note: A blocky night city built around one plaza: the TOYS shop row (west), the gold VIP 5,000+ lounge (east), the Spire with its TOP HELPERS leaderboard (north) and the canal footbridge (south). Colour script: cold blue loneliness → burning red disaster → warm gold at the end.
outline: ECU red 0 + on-screen hook text; reveal the face under it.
Sea of thousands; VIP rope; shop door slammed; kid backs away; whispers; staged help ticks +1 only when phones rise. Plant: why won't mine move?
Offers help in public — refused/mocked ('a zero can't be trusted'); funny-sad box catch by a VIP on camera; one tender bench scene with Guest (meter 2).
Alone at night he fixes a bridge plank and returns a lost pet toy. The 0 glitches to gold ∞ for exactly 2 frames. VIP help stops the instant the phone drops.
SERVER EVENT: METEOR STORM. Red sky, first impact on the plaza, signs tear off, crowds stampede, the Spire cracks and leans.
VIPs grab legendary pets and run past people who need help; numbers flicker. 'Move, zero!' — shoved down. Guest pinned under the Spire. Everyone passes.
Countdown to the next impact. Dig, lift, slip, fall, get up, lift. 'Your number's not going up.' 'Doesn't matter.' Meteor #2 hits the Spire as they clear it.
Silence. The red 0 cracks and flips to a gold ∞ in slow motion. The crowd stares. The meter only counted help with an audience. VIP numbers drain red.
The shopkeeper holds the door. Guest takes his hand. Push-in on ∞. Last line. Black.
draft:
DRAFT v1 (rejected)
NARRATOR: Everyone in Bricktown has a kindness number.
NARRATOR: Mine is zero. Nobody knows why.
NARRATOR: The rich kids have thousands and they show it off.
NARRATOR: One day meteors started falling from the sky.
NARRATOR: Everyone ran away to save their pets.
NARRATOR: I saved a little kid who was stuck.
NARRATOR: My number turned into infinity because I was a true hero all along.
NARRATOR: The end. Be kind!
critique: HOOK — v1 opens on exposition ('Everyone in Bricktown has…'). No image, no stakes. FIX: open on an ECU of the red 0 with the full rule as an on-screen card; first spoken words land the sting ('mine was stuck at zero').
TELL vs SHOW — v1 narrates every event. FIX: narrator only bridges; the rule is SHOWN (door slam, kid backing away, a +1 that only ticks when phones rise).

TWIST FAIRNESS — v1's infinity comes from nowhere ('true hero all along'). FIX: plant it twice: (1) the 0 glitches to ∞ for exactly 2 frames when he helps unseen; (2) VIP numbers only tick under cameras and help stops when the phone drops. The payoff line names the mechanism: the meter counted audiences.

MIDDLE SAG — v1 jumps from 'shows it off' to meteors. FIX: a public-help attempt that fails comically (box catch on camera, 'literally over your head'), then one tender beat (Guest, meter 2) so we care who gets trapped later.
STAKES — v1 rescue is one line. FIX: countdown overlay, a slip and fall (near-failure), the Spire leaning, a second meteor, and the kid telling him his number isn't moving ('Doesn't matter').

EMOTION — v1 ends on a moral. FIX: silence before the flip; nobody speaks at the payoff; the shopkeeper who slammed the door now holds it; a quotable last line that reframes the title ('the only kind that counts').

ESCALATION CADENCE — every 10-15 s there is a new reveal: door slam (0:11), +1 under cameras (0:19), the mock (0:35), Guest (0:42), 2-frame glitch (0:58), phone-drop (1:03), red sky (1:06), impact (1:12), Spire (1:22), shove (1:32), pinned kid (1:38), countdown (1:52), slip (1:58), meteor #2 (2:06), flip (2:14), numbers fall (2:20), door (2:27).
rewrites: v2: added the plank + pet-toy clue scene, the camera-only VIP plant, Guest's bench scene, the shove.

v3: cut 30% of narration words; replaced 'true hero' with the audience mechanism; moved 'Turns out…' to a title card in his voice; made the payoff wordless except the last line; 'You're welcome!' and 'literally over your head' added as the two comic beats; last line rewritten from 'Be kind' to 'That's the only kind that counts.'

self_check.Is the hook sharp?: Yes — a pulsing red 0 in ECU plus the rule in one card, and the sting in the first spoken line.
self_check.Is the twist fair and surprising?: Fair: planted twice (2-frame ∞ glitch, +1 only under cameras). Surprising: the audience assumes he never helped; the film shows he only ever helped unseen.
self_check.Does the clue pay off?: Yes — the exact ∞ glyph from the 2-frame glitch is what the 0 becomes; the camera-only plant pays off when the VIP numbers drain.
self_check.Does the middle ever sag?: No beat runs longer than ~12 s without a new reveal or turn (see cadence list).
self_check.Does it make people feel something?: Rejection → tenderness (bench) → injustice (shove, everyone passing) → effort and near-failure → silence → release (gold ∞, held door, taken hand).
